tasks.summary: Implement the first owner/admin Site Settings and admin profile CRUD surface.
acceptance: CMS managers can inspect and save the default site settings through /admin/settings.
CMS managers can invite new CMS users and grant/update CMS access for existing login accounts through /admin/settings.
CMS access form validation catches duplicate login account IDs and duplicate normalized access emails before save.
Website owner assignment and Website owner access changes are owner-protected in UI and RLS; no destructive profile delete controls are shown.
Viewer/editor users can inspect but not save global settings in the UI.
Supabase RLS write policies for site_settings require owner/admin roles.
Supabase RLS policies for admin_profiles prevent admin users from changing owner profiles or assigning owner role.
Supabase admin_profiles enforces case-insensitive normalized email uniqueness.
Anonymous users cannot directly execute admin SECURITY DEFINER helper functions.
The form includes loading, empty, validation, save, success, read-only, and error states.
No service-role key is shipped to browser code.

A safe Published settings change made through /admin/settings persists after refresh and is read back through the supported public footer/contact/social/default SEO consumer, then is restored or otherwise documented.
Supabase Auth custom SMTP and the exact production invite/recovery account-setup Redirect URLs are configured and verified before account handoff is called available.
An approved new editor receives the Settings invite, sets a password, signs out, and signs back in with that password.
The approved editor receives a password-recovery email, sets a new password, verifies the old password fails, and signs in with the new password.

Supabase MCP: execute_sql verifies site_settings write policies require owner/admin
